articles.title: 'Board accepted his resignation': Nvidia chairman rules out Jensen Huang's return; company doubles revenue
articles.summary: Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones on Tuesday ruled out Jensen Huang's return, saying the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.
articles.body: Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones on Tuesday ruled out Jensen Huang's return, saying the board does not intend to reinstate him as CEO.The company's revenue, meanwhile, soared more than 100% year-on-year.Also Read | Nvidia Q3 results: Revenue jumps 103% to $115.8 billion; announces $0.25 per-share dividend"The board of directors unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said at the start of Nvidia's quarterly earnings call.His statement came hours after Huang expressed his desire to return to the company if invited.Huang, who left Nvidia last week following revelations of an extramarital affair and other alleged relationships, made his first public comments since his departure in a social media post. Acknowledging "serious mistakes" in his personal life, he said he would be "honoured" to return if the board believed it was in the best interests of the company, its shareholders, employees and the country.His possible return had drawn support from several technology industry figures, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. US President Donald Trump has also backed his reinstatement, saying the Taiwan-born executive had "learned a big lesson".An online petition urging Nvidia's board to reinstate Huang has attracted support from current and former employees, investors and other Silicon Valley figures. Its organisers questioned whether his departure had followed due process and called for an independent investigation into the allegations.Nvidia earnings double; report makes no mention of HuangMeanwhile, Nvidia made no mention of Huang's departure or possible return in its third-quarter earnings statement released on Tuesday.The chipmaker reported revenue of more than $116 billion, double the figure from a year earlier and above Wall Street estimates. Net income stood at $2.70 per share, beating analysts' expectations of $2.48.Chief financial officer Colette Kress was expected to address Wall Street analysts on the earnings call for the first time since being named interim CEO following Huang's departure.His exit followed revelation of a relationships with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected of having links to Beijing's intelligence services and a senior Nvidia executive who reported to him.The businesswoman was an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed International, which is under US investigation for allegedly violating export controls by diverting advanced Nvidia AI chips to Chinese companies.(With AP inputs)Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: PM discusses trade with leaders of 3 SE Asian nations
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met the Philippines President, Ferdinand Marcos, on the margins of the Asean and East Asia Summit, welcoming the increased
articles.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met the Philippines President, Ferdinand Marcos, on the margins of the Asean and East Asia Summit, welcoming the increased momentum in bilateral cooperation in areas such as defence and security, space, railway infrastructure, fintech, and trade and investment under the Strategic Partnership established between the two countries last year.The two leaders also exchanged views on key regional and global issues of mutual interest, according to a ministry of external affairs (MEA) readout."The Prime Minister congratulated the Philippines on its successful chairship of ASEAN this year. He appreciated the role of the Philippines as country coordinator for India in the ASEAN since 2024 and its continued support in strengthening ASEAN-India relations," said the ministry.Modi also met his counterparts from Singapore and Thailand, Lawrence Wong and Anutin Charnvirakul, respectively.In the meeting with Wong, the leaders discussed the way forward across the eight priority areas: economic cooperation, skills development, digitalisation, sustainability, connectivity, healthcare and medicine, defence and security cooperation, and people-to-people and cultural exchanges. As Singapore prepares to assume Asean chairship, Modi assured Wong of full support from India.With the Thai PM, Modi discussed trade and investment, defence and security, connectivity, digital technologies and fintech, culture, tourism and people-to-people ties."The leaders also underscored the importance of working closely together in regional forums such as BIMSTEC, IORA, Mekong Ganga Cooperation and the ASEAN-led architecture. Both leaders also exchanged views on various regional and global issues of mutual importance and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening their partnership," said the ministry.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Nvidia Q3 results: Revenue jumps 103% to $115.8 billion; announces $0.25 per-share dividend
articles.summary: Nvidia Q3 results: Nvidia investors finally have something to cheer about as the chipmaker reported a blockbuster third quarter, with revenue soaring more
articles.body: Nvidia Q3 results: Nvidia investors finally have something to cheer about as the chipmaker reported a blockbuster third quarter, with revenue soaring more than 100% year-on-year.The company reported revenue of $115.8 billion for the third quarter ended October 25, 2026, marking a 103% increase from the year-ago period and a 20% rise from the previous quarter. Its GAAP earnings per diluted share stood at $2.70, while non-GAAP earnings per diluted share came in at $2.68.The timing of the results is particularly significant as the tech giant is caught up in a series of controversies surrounding its former boss, Jensen Huang, alleged to have had a relationship with a Chinese ‘spy’, apart from two other women.Also Read| As Nvidia founder Jensen Hunag says, he is ready to come back as CEO; Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says board has determined it will not reinstate Huang and that is Board'sNvidia Q3 resultsThe company reported GAAP gross margins of 74.8% and non-GAAP gross margins of 74.9% for the quarter. Nvidia also returned $28.1 billion to shareholders during the third quarter of fiscal 2027 through share buybacks and cash dividends.Back in September 2026, Nvidia's Board of Directors approved an additional $150 billion in share repurchase authorisation, with no expiration date. At the end of the third quarter, approximately $227.3 billion remained available under the programme.Nvidia's next quarterly cash dividend will be $0.25 per share, payable on December 23, 2026, to shareholders on record as of December 2, 2026.Commenting on the quarterly performance, Colette Kress, interim CEO and executive vice president and chief financial officer of Nvidia, highlighted the company's continued momentum and technology leadership.“Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in a press statement.She also expressed confidence in the company's technology roadmap, adding, “Vera Rubin is off to an explosive start, our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater."Jensen Huang admits mistakes, signals willingness to returnWhile Nvidia's financial performance remained in focus, former CEO Jensen Huang made his first public comments since being caught up in the alleged Chinese Spy Scandal.In a statement on X, Huang thanked those who had supported him and his family over the past week. He also spoke about his journey to the United States and described becoming an American citizen as one of the proudest moments of his life."Over the past week, I’ve been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life."Huang described Nvidia as his life's work and said building the company alongside his colleagues had been a privilege. He also acknowledged that his personal conduct had fallen short of the standards expected at the company and said he regretted the difficulties caused to its board."Nvidia has been my life’s work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honour. Nowhere but in America could a company like Nvidia be possible. I love our country, and I love Nvidia. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board’s independent investigation," he added.His statement also signalled his willingness to return as the company's chief executive if the board backed his reinstatement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he said.Board refuses to bring back HuangHowever, any possibility of Huang returning to the leadership role was ruled out by Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones. Speaking at the beginning of the company's quarterly earnings call on Tuesday, Jones said the board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and had no intention of bringing him back as CEO."The board of directors unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," Jones said.The chairman's remarks came just hours after Huang indicated that he would be open to returning to the company if invited.The controversy centres on Huang's alleged relationship with Alice Huang, the alleged Chinese Spy. The former CEO resigned last week following revelations of extramarital affairs, including one involving a Chinese woman who worked at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company.The allegations have also brought scrutiny to relationships linked to Huang both within and outside Nvidia. His latest statement acknowledged personal mistakes and expressed his commitment to cooperating with the board's independent investigation.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Fairfax to sell 13% via 3.4k cr block deal, exit IIFL Finance
articles.summary: Mumbai: Canada's Fairfax Group, which is in the process of acquiring IDBI Bank, is selling its entire 13.3% stake in IIFL Finance through a block deal
articles.body: Mumbai: Canada's Fairfax Group, which is in the process of acquiring IDBI Bank, is selling its entire 13.3% stake in IIFL Finance through a block deal worth about Rs 3,450 crore (around $370 million). FIH Mauritius Investments, an arm of Fairfax, has mandated IIFL Capital, a group company, to sell over 5.6 crore shares of IIFL Finance on Wednesday, Nov 18, a term sheet for the deal showed.While Fairfax is exiting IIFL Finance, it continues to hold 38% in IIFL Capital, currently worth about Rs 4,200 crore, shareholding data on BSE showed.The block of IIFL Finance shares is being sold at a floor price of Rs 611 per share, a 3.9% discount to the stock's closing price of Rs 636 on BSE on Tuesday.A little over a month back, Canada-headquartered Fairfax Financial Holdings said that it had entered a deal to acquire a nearly 61% stake in IDBI Bank for Rs 53,000 crore. Since the announcement of the deal, it was expected that the Canadian financial services group would exit some of its holdings in India, mainly to part-finance the IDBI Bank stake acquisition.On Oct 15, the cabinet committee on economic affairs approved an arm of Fairfax to buy a 30.5% stake held by govt for Rs 26,620 crore and another 30.2% from LIC for Rs 26,440 crore.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: iPhone shipments drop 25%, Samsung regains top spot
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Apple's iPhone shipments in India fell 25% in July-Sept.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Apple's iPhone shipments in India fell 25% in July-Sept. The company shipped about 3.7 million iPhones, down from a record 5 million a year earlier, according to IDC. Samsung overtook Vivo to reclaim the top spot after 10 quarters, emerging as the only brand among the top 10 to ship more phones than it did a year ago.IDC attributed Apple's decline to shortages of iPhone 15, 16 and 17, fewer discounts on older models and price increases around the Sept launch. The pricier iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max together made up more than 30% of Apple's quarterly shipments, with no base iPhone 18 model on sale. Apple moved back to fourth place as several rivals posted steeper declines.Samsung's shipments rose 7.9%, lifting its market share to 17.7% from 12.6% a year earlier. IDC said Samsung had raised prices more gradually than rivals in the first half of the year and benefited from a wider range of models. Vivo's shipments fell 29.9%, leaving it in second place with a 16.8% share. Oppo held third place as its shipments fell 26.5%.Overall smartphone shipments fell 23.3% to 36.8 million units, making it India's weakest festive quarter in a decade, according to IDC. Retailers cut back on new orders as higher memory chip costs pushed up phone prices and left brands less room to offer festive discounts. Shipments to offline retailers fell 26.7%, compared with an 18.9% decline online. Phones priced below $100 took the biggest hit. Shipments fell 90.9% to 700,000 units, cutting the segment's share to 1.9% from 16.2% a year earlier. The average selling price rose 26.1% to a record $371, while the overall value of the market fell 3.3%."Higher ASPs, thin discounts and longer replacement cycles kept demand subdued even through the festive period," said Upasana Joshi, senior research manager at IDC Asia Pacific. IDC expects the decline to deepen in Oct-Dec, with shipments projected to fall more than 25% year on year as stocks of cheaper phones run down. It forecasts full-year shipments of 125-127 million units, down 16-18% from 2025.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.
